rationale: Both candidates map cleanly to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis), but PGS000704 has better endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported exactly “Alcoholic cirrhosis” vs PGS001777’s restricted “Cirrhosis (males)”) and a much stronger, more PRS-like construction (183,271 variants via snpnet vs 3-variant GWAS-hit score). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC/C-index are not directly comparable; still, PGS000704’s basic covariates (age-as-timescale, sex, PCs, batch) are transparent and non-leaky, whereas PGS001777’s covariates are unknown and its reported AUROC is explicitly full-model. Given the stronger genome-wide model and cleaner phenotype/covariate specification, PGS000704 is better supported overall despite PGS001777’s larger OR(top vs bottom quintile).

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = abdominal aortic aneurysm), same method (PRS-CS), same variant count (1,118,997), and same evaluation ancestry (EUR only), so endpoint fidelity and structural properties do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (pgs_only_* are null), so the full-model metrics are not clean PRS-comparable; however, PGS003973 at least discloses basic demographic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) alongside a higher concordance/C-index (0.882) whereas PGS003972 has covariates listed as Unknown with a lower full-model AUROC (0.69). Given otherwise indistinguishable records, the combination of transparent (and non-leaky) covariates plus stronger reported discrimination makes PGS003973 the slightly better-supported choice, but confidence is low because the key PRS-only performance metrics are missing for both.

Both candidates map to the target trait (trait_efo=arthritis), but PGS001135 has substantially cleaner, PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R²=0.00291 (and incremental AUROC=0.00314) with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and these PRS-only metrics are plausibly below the trait heritability ceiling. In contrast, PGS004547 provides no AUROC/R² at all (only an OR=1.26, which is weak-to-moderate) and has unknown covariates, while also being a risk-factor integration/metaPRS style model that raises comparability concerns. Although PGS004547 uses many more variants and a larger validation N, the lack of PRS-only metrics and unclear covariate/packaging make it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001135.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ankylosing spondylitis) and both use only basic demographic/PC-style covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). The key differentiator is performance evidence: PGS001267 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R2=0.0988) enabling a direct PRS-quality assessment and a heritability-ceiling sanity check, whereas PGS002089 provides no AUROC/R2 and only a partial correlation (0.0919), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination. Although PGS002089 has many more variants and a larger training N, the missing PRS-comparable metrics make it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001267.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo and identical phenotyping_reported: DSM-5 AUD criteria count, log-transformed), method (PRS-CS), ancestry (EUR GWAS/EVAL), and training cohort (UKB). The differentiators are performance and evidence strength: PGS000201 shows a materially higher incremental signal (ΔR² 0.01192 vs 0.00456) and a stronger effect size (β=0.099, SE=0.01 vs β=0.043, SE=0.019), consistent with better PRS contribution. Although PGS000201 uses a slightly heavier but still basic covariate set (adds array/site), this is not strong leakage and does not outweigh its stronger PRS-associated metrics; validation N differences are a weak tie-break. Therefore PGS000201 is better supported on the visible PRS-relevant evidence.

PGS005254 is the better-supported match to the target trait (aortic stenosis): it has exact trait_reported/trait_efo alignment to aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is labeled as “Mean pressure gradient” with a broader/mixed trait_efo (“aortic stenosis, aortic measurement”), making it more measurement-anchored despite sharing the same phenotyping_reported (incident aortic stenosis). Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, PRS-CS, EUR-only dev/eval, identical covariates, same validation N=244,450, and no PRS-only AUC/R2), so the decision falls to endpoint/label fidelity and available effect-size evidence; PGS005254 also shows a slightly stronger HR per SD (1.64 vs 1.53).

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (same trait_reported/trait_efo). However, PGS003972 is supported by a large disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis context (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.1M variants, which is structurally more likely to capture polygenic signal than PGS000753’s sparse P+T score with 29 variants. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, and PGS003972’s only visible AUROC (0.69) is a full-model metric with unknown covariates so it can’t be treated as PRS-comparable; still, PGS000753 also lacks PRS-only metrics and only offers a moderate OR=1.37. PGS000753 has cleaner disclosed covariates (age/sex/PCs) and broader eval ancestry, but the much stronger methodological/coverage signals and broader disease-study development context favor PGS003972 overall.

PGS001268 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7346 and PGS-only R²=0.10232 (with CIs for AUROC) under basic covariates, enabling a clean PRS assessment and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. PGS002089 lacks PRS-only AUC/R² entirely and provides only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919), which is less directly comparable as a PRS performance metric. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (ankylosing spondylitis), but PGS001268’s time-to-event phenotyping is a mild mismatch versus generic disease status, partially offset by its broader multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS) compared with PGS002089’s EUR/GME/SAS. Given the missing core PRS metrics for PGS002089, PGS001268 has the stronger visible support despite being from a pan-trait sparse-score framework.

PGS002738 is the better match to the target trait alcohol dependence on endpoint fidelity: its trait_efo is exactly "alcohol dependence" and both trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are "Alcohol use disorder" (a direct clinical diagnosis construct). PGS000201 is more weakly aligned conceptually (trait_reported "Problematic alcohol use" and trait_efo "alcohol dependence measurement"), suggesting a more quantitative/problem-use phenotype rather than dependence itself. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS002738 provides a reasonably strong case-enrichment effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96), whereas PGS000201 only shows a small incremental ΔR²=0.01192 (and a beta on a transformed criteria-count outcome), which is harder to interpret as dependence risk discrimination. Covariates in PGS000201 are basic and clean, while PGS002738 has unknown covariates (a confidence penalty), but overall the stronger endpoint match plus stronger effect-size signal favors PGS002738.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper with identical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and similar ancestry setup, so the decision rests on endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metrics. PGS001261 uses a time-to-event (TTE) angina endpoint, which is a mild mismatch for a generic angina pectoris target compared with PGS001262’s direct doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype. On comparable PRS-only metrics, PGS001262 is slightly stronger (PGS-only AUROC 0.5868 vs 0.5823; PGS-only R² 0.0130 vs 0.0123) and both are below the heritability ceiling, so PGS001262 has the cleaner phenotype alignment plus marginally better PRS-only performance. PGS001261’s only notable advantage is larger training N and more variants, but those are weaker signals here than endpoint fidelity and PRS-only discrimination.

PGS005252 is the better-supported match to the target trait (aortic stenosis): its trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are directly aligned to incident aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is primarily a valve-function quantitative trait score (trait_reported="Mean pressure gradient"; trait_efo includes "aortic measurement"), making endpoint fidelity weaker despite mentioning incident AS in phenotyping. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect-size evidence is key: PGS005252 shows a stronger HR per SD (1.92 vs 1.53 for PGS005255). Although PGS005252 reports only a full-model C-index 0.87 with heavy clinical covariates (limiting comparability), PGS005255 provides no discrimination metric at all; with similar EUR-only evaluation and similar variant counts, the direct disease targeting plus stronger HR favors PGS005252.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R² (0.00291) with basic covariates, allowing a clean PRS signal check (and it stays below the provided heritability ceiling). PGS004477 has an arthritis-mapped ICD10-style endpoint (“M13 Other arthritis”) and a genome-wide LDpred2 build with an OR (~1.20), but it provides no PRS-comparable AUC/R² at all and has unknown covariates, making its predictive performance and comparability much less verifiable from the record. While PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework (a negative), the absence of usable performance metrics for PGS004477 leaves PGS001135 as the more evidentially grounded choice here.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (same trait_reported/trait_efo). However, PGS003973 is better supported structurally and by study context: it is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with ~1.12M variants developed across many cohorts (ARIC, HUNT, deCODE, eMERGE, MVP, etc.), which is generally more capable of capturing polygenic signal than the very sparse P+T score in PGS000753 (29 variants). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the only visible discrimination metric for PGS003973 (C-index 0.882) is a full-model value and cannot be treated as PRS-comparable; still, its covariates are basic (age/age^2/sex) and not obviously leakage-heavy. PGS000753 does provide an OR per SD (1.37, moderate), but lacks any comparable PRS-only metrics and is based on a much smaller, hits-only model; overall the multi-cohort, genome-wide construction in PGS003973 outweighs the modest OR evidence in PGS000753.

PGS004913 has cleaner endpoint fidelity to the target: both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis,” matching the alcoholic liver cirrhosis EFO, whereas PGS001777’s phenotyping_reported is “Cirrhosis (males),” a broader/sex-restricted phenotype that is less directly aligned to alcohol-related cirrhosis. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R², but PGS004913 at least reports a PRS-associated effect size (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), while PGS001777’s only AUROC is a full-model AUROC (0.671) that is not PRS-comparable and its covariates are unknown, making its performance evidence harder to interpret. Structurally, PGS004913 also uses more variants (20 vs 3), which is a modest positive signal when PRS-only metrics are absent.

PGS002738 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_efo is exactly "alcohol dependence" and both trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are "Alcohol use disorder" (a close clinical synonym). It also shows stronger PRS signal in the visible metrics (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 [1.54–2.51]) compared with PGS000202’s very small incremental ΔR² (0.00456) and small beta (0.043). While PGS002738 has unknown covariates (a weakness), PGS000202’s mapped trait is "alcohol dependence measurement" and trait_reported is "Problematic alcohol use," which is less endpoint-faithful to dependence than a disorder diagnosis, even though its covariates are cleanly specified. Both are EUR-evaluated and use PRS-CS; variant count favors PGS000202, but the endpoint fidelity and stronger effect-size evidence favor PGS002738 overall.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo are aortic stenosis; both are incident aortic stenosis in EUR DEV/EVAL) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must lean on effect-size evidence and covariate comparability. PGS005254 reports a clear per-SD HR=1.64 with CI (1.50–1.78) under a basic covariate set (age, age^2, sex, PCs), making its PRS signal more interpretable. PGS005252 reports a higher HR (1.92) but without CI and its only discrimination metric is a full-model C-index=0.87 alongside a much heavier comorbidity/clinical covariate bundle (T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), which risks covariate-driven inflation and is not PRS-comparable. Given cleaner evaluation context and better-specified effect-size uncertainty, PGS005254 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper, with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (269,704), covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), ancestry distribution, and validation size (24,905), so the decision rests on endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metrics. PGS001261 is more endpoint-specific to the target trait via its time-to-event angina pectoris phenotyping (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported explicitly ‘Angina pectoris (time-to-event)’), whereas PGS001260 is the vaguer ‘Angina’. PGS001261 also has marginally better PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.58233 vs 0.58108; PGS-only R2 0.01228 vs 0.01185; slightly higher incremental AUROC 0.00796 vs 0.00783). Differences are small, hence moderate confidence, but they consistently favor PGS001261.

PGS001267 is the better match to the target trait as a generic ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both ‘Ankylosing spondylitis’), whereas PGS001268 is explicitly a time-to-event (TTE) formulation (‘Ankylosing spondylitis (time-to-event)’, ‘TTE ankylosing spondylitis’), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic disease target. Both are otherwise near-clones (same pan-trait UKB framework publication, same snpnet method, 10 variants, same EUR-only training and identical covariates and validation size/ancestry mix). Although PGS001268 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 (0.7346/0.1023 vs 0.7265/0.0988), the metric gap is small and doesn’t outweigh the cleaner endpoint alignment of PGS001267; both R2 values remain well below the heritability ceiling, so heritability doesn’t differentiate them.

Both candidates are from the same UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet framework paper, share the same mapped trait (EFO: angina pectoris), identical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and similar ancestry setup (DEV EUR; multi-ancestry EVAL with selected EUR record), so endpoint/covariate comparability is essentially matched. On PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001262 is modestly stronger than PGS001260 (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683 vs 0.58108; PGS-only R² 0.01304 vs 0.01185), and both remain below the provided h2_obs ceiling (~0.009–0.014 range) at a similar order of magnitude, without obvious inflation. Although PGS001260 has a larger training N and more variants, within this same-method sibling comparison the directly reported PRS-only performance favors PGS001262, making it the better-supported choice.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are alcoholic liver cirrhosis/cirrhosis). However, PGS004913 is a disease-focused score explicitly developed for alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, with clean basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and provides PRS-relevant effect evidence (OR top vs bottom decile = 4.4) plus an R² estimate (0.029, though not explicitly labeled PGS-only). PGS000704 comes from a broad UKB biomarker genetics framework paper and only reports a full-model time-to-event C-index (0.711) with no PGS-only AUC/R²; its per-SD HR is modest (1.18), making the apparent discrimination likely covariate-driven and weaker PRS signal. Despite PGS000704’s much larger training/validation and variant count, the more endpoint-targeted evidence and stronger PRS effect size support PGS004913.

PGS001344 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance and endpoint specificity: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.64568) and PGS-only R² (0.05973) for a clearly defined phenotype (“Asthma diagnosed by doctor”), with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). In contrast, PGS001782 has no PGS-only AUROC (only a full-model AUROC=0.659 is shown, which is not comparable as a PRS metric), and its PRS-comparable metric is a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 with a more generic phenotype label (“Asthma”). While PGS001782 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method and multi-biobank GWAS context, the missing PRS-only AUROC and less specific phenotyping make its visible evidence weaker than PGS001344’s cleaner PRS-only metric package.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same reported/phenotyped trait (M13 Other arthritis), same EFO mapping (arthritis), same training cohort (UKB), same EUR-only development/evaluation, same training (n=174,489) and validation size (n=56,192), and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only OR reported). With metrics otherwise missing, the main differentiator is the available PRS effect size: PGS004547 reports a higher OR per SD (1.262) than PGS004477 (1.196), indicating stronger PRS signal. Method-wise, PGS004547’s RFDiseasemetaPRS suggests multi-score aggregation, which is a positive structural signal versus the single-score LDpred2 in PGS004477, reinforcing the choice. Confidence is moderate because neither provides PGS-only AUC/R2 and covariates are unknown for both.

PGS004587 is the better-supported match to the target trait (atopic eczema) because its endpoint is a general atopic dermatitis diagnosis framed as incident disease (phenotyping_reported: "Incident atopic dermatitis"), aligning well with generic atopic eczema risk, whereas PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype ("Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis"), which is a phenotype restriction relative to the target. Neither record provides PRS-comparable performance (no PGS-only AUC/R2 for either); PGS001773’s very high AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 appear to be full-model metrics and are further confounded by inclusion of parental ethnicity covariates, so they are not clean evidence of PRS strength and the R² is implausibly high versus the eczema heritability ceiling. PGS004587 at least reports a PRS-stratified HR (1.153 high vs low), and is evaluated at much larger scale in EUR (n=337,910) with standard demographic/SES covariates, making its evidence package more coherent for the target despite modest effect size.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_efo=atopic eczema; phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis), use the same basic covariates, and have identical EUR evaluation size (n=337,910), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either—so metrics don’t differentiate beyond similar HRs (PGS002755 HR=1.249 vs PGS004587 HR=1.153). The main differentiator is structural PRS quality: PGS002755 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is generally better suited for a polygenic trait like atopic eczema than PGS004587’s 23 genome-wide significant SNPs. With endpoints and evaluation context essentially tied, the higher-capacity genome-wide model is better-supported.

PGS002727 is from a disease-focused pediatric asthma study (“Multiancestral polygenic risk score for pediatric asthma”) with explicit endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma) and a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; ~986k variants) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57), and it reports evaluation across multiple ancestries. PGS001344, while having clean PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.6457; PGS-only R2=0.0597, below the asthma h2 ceiling) and basic covariates, comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) using a very sparse snpnet model (6,139 variants), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external generalization. Because PGS002727’s reported AUROC/R2 appear to be full-model only (so not directly comparable), the decision rests mainly on endpoint/study archetype and structural signals, favoring the disease-focused, genome-wide PRS002727 over the framework sparse PGS001344.

Both candidates align to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo = asthma). However, PGS001782 provides a clearly PRS-comparable performance metric: a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R² (pgs_only_r2=0.048844) plus AUROC=0.659 with explicitly basic covariates (sex, age, 20 PCs). This R² is interpretable against the asthma heritability ceiling (well below h2_liability=0.1515), giving cleaner evidence of PRS signal. In contrast, PGS002727 reports only full-model metrics (AUROC=0.66, R²=0.04) with covariates listed as Unknown, so its discrimination cannot be attributed to the PRS alone; despite a strong OR=1.57 and broader multi-ancestry evaluation, the lack of PRS-only/adjusted metrics makes its support less clean. Therefore PGS001782 is better-supported on the visible, comparable PRS evidence.

PGS001263 is a direct endpoint match to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Atrial flutter”), and it reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R2=0.025) with basic covariates; its PGS-only R2 is also plausibly below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0157), supporting metric sanity. PGS002050 has a broader phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) rather than flutter-specific, and it lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 entirely (only partial correlation reported), making its predictive evidence less directly comparable for atrial flutter despite higher variant count and training N.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the shared full-model AUROC=0.632 is not a differentiator. The only visible performance separation is slightly stronger association for PGS000454 (top 1% vs rest OR 3.79 vs 3.61; marginally higher Nagelkerke R² 0.0489 vs 0.0487) with essentially identical per-SD OR. Given the minimal differences and non-PRS-only metrics, confidence is low, but PGS000454 has the small edge in effect-size evidence.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the visible full-model AUROC/C-index values are not comparable PRS metrics. PGS005168 is heavily penalized by explicit clinical risk-calculator packaging in covariates (includes CHARGE-AF), making its high C-index (0.8718) likely covariate-driven and weak evidence about standalone PRS quality. PGS002814 uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding that leakage concern, and still shows strong effect size (OR≈1.94 per SD). While PGS005168 has a stronger shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and far more variants, the CHARGE-AF packaging undermines interpretability enough that the cleaner, more PRS-comparable evaluation setup of PGS002814 narrowly wins.

PGS002755 is a closer match to the target trait as a general atopic dermatitis/atopic eczema endpoint (incident atopic dermatitis) and is evaluated at very large scale in EUR (n=337,910) with a PRS-specific effect size reported (HR high vs low PRS=1.249). In contrast, PGS001773 targets a narrower phenotype (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis) and its only reported discrimination is a very high AUROC/R² that appears to be full-model (not PGS-only) and is likely influenced by covariates including parental ethnicity; with no PGS-only metrics, that 0.93 AUROC is not comparable evidence of PRS strength. Despite PGS002755 also lacking PGS-only AUC/R², its genome-wide PRS-CS construction (1,090,702 variants) and cleaner PRS-relevant signal plus broader GWAS ancestry support make it better-supported overall than the 25-variant, covariate-inflated full-model report in PGS001773.

Both candidates are near-clones for basal cell carcinoma: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are not strong PRS-comparable evidence. Given this near-tie, PGS000454 has a marginal edge on the visible evaluation metrics (slightly higher full-model AUROC 0.632 vs 0.630 and higher Nagelkerke R² 0.0489 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456’s slightly higher top-1% OR does not outweigh the overall similarity.

Both candidates target the same combined endpoint (trait_efo includes atrial flutter; phenotyping_reported is atrial fibrillation and flutter), so endpoint fidelity is essentially tied, though PGS001339 is explicitly time-to-event. The key differentiator is performance evidence: PGS001339 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.613 and PGS-only R²=0.02447), which are interpretable and below the local h2_obs ceiling (~0.0157) only modestly (suggesting at least a usable PRS signal, while full-model AUROC is clearly covariate-boosted). In contrast, PGS002050 provides no PRS-only AUROC/R² at all and only a partial correlation (0.1034), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination ranking. Although PGS002050 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with far more variants and slightly larger training N, the missing PRS-comparable metrics make it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001339.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait/phenotyping (basal cell carcinoma), same EFO, same method (GWAS Hits), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are not a clean PRS comparator and are essentially noise (0.632 vs 0.630). As a weak tie-break within this identical design, PGS000452 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0487 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456’s higher top-1% OR does not clearly outweigh those small differences. Given the minimal separability and lack of PRS-only metrics, confidence is low.

PGS000327 has clean endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to autism spectrum disorder, whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is explicitly different ("Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)"), a major mismatch for an ASD target despite the ASD label fields. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², but PGS000327 provides a meaningful effect size (OR=1.33 per SD) and a higher reported R² (0.0245 vs partial R²=0.00546 for PGS002790), consistent with stronger PRS signal. Study context also favors PGS000327 as a disease-focused multi-cohort ASD GWAS paper with stated training n=28,592 and EUR-only evaluation, while PGS002790 lacks training sample size (N/A) and appears to come from a broader cross-trait/sex-specific association study, increasing risk that the score is not optimized for ASD diagnosis.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUCs are not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS005168’s reported C-index=0.8718 is explicitly conditioned on a strong clinical risk-calculator covariate (CHARGE-AF), which is a major packaging/leakage concern and makes its performance evidence largely non-informative for standalone PRS quality. PGS005313 uses only basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding that risk-wrapper penalty, and it provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.82) supportive of PRS discrimination; it also uses a cross-ancestry PRS-CSx construction with much larger variant coverage. Despite PGS005168 having broader cohort listing and a large validation set, the CHARGE-AF adjustment is the decisive negative, so PGS005313 is better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS001263 is the better match to the target trait (atrial flutter) with direct endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all specifically “Atrial flutter,” whereas PGS001339 is a combined and time-to-event phenotype (“atrial fibrillation and flutter (time-to-event)”), which is a less clean match for a generic atrial flutter target. On PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001263 is also slightly stronger (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.02517 vs 0.02447), with similar basic covariates, identical training sample size and validation size, and similarly broad evaluation ancestries. Given the near-clone study context, the decision is driven mainly by endpoint specificity plus the small PRS-only metric edge for PGS001263.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the listed AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable as standalone PRS metrics. Given that, structural and transportability signals dominate: PGS005313 uses PRS-CSx with genome-wide coverage (1,271,239 variants) and is developed from a broader multi-cohort set (includes MVP and SIMPLER in addition to AFGen/BBJ/FinnGen/UKB/deCODE etc.) with multi-ancestry GWAS inputs and multi-ancestry evaluation noted, plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.82). PGS002814 is a sparse P+T score with far fewer variants (4,520) and evaluation restricted to East Asian only; while it reports OR ~1.94 and an R2=0.14, that R2 is not clearly PRS-only and is unusually high for a simple thresholding approach, making it less reliable as comparative evidence. PGS004254 is the better-supported Crohn’s disease PRS on endpoint fidelity and PRS signal strength: it targets a direct Crohn’s disease diagnosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both Crohn’s disease) and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.18), consistent with meaningful PRS discrimination, using only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). In contrast, PGS001330 comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with a time-to-event phenotype and shows weak PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC=0.576; PGS R2=0.0062), well below the trait’s heritability ceiling and indicative of limited standalone PRS utility despite larger training size and multi-ancestry evaluation. PGS004254 lacks explicit PGS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC=0.72), which lowers certainty, but the combination of direct endpoint and much stronger OR outweighs the framework-score’s modest PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates align well to the target depressive disorder (trait_efo=major depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported is MDD in both), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R²—only small full-model/unspecified R² (~0.022 for PGS003333 vs ~0.0241 for PGS003576), so performance evidence is weak and largely non-comparable. Given that, structural/transport signals break the tie: PGS003576 has explicit basic covariates (PCs 1–10) and substantially broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/AMR/ASN/EAS/EUR) plus a larger genome-wide variant set (5.8M vs 1.1M), whereas PGS003333 has unknown covariates and EUR-only evaluation. The slight R² edge and cleaner covariate disclosure favor PGS003576.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo=major depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported is a direct depression/MDD endpoint) and are EUR-trained/EUR-evaluated with similar genome-wide PRS-CS-style methods and ~1.09M variants. The key differentiator is performance evidence: PGS002759 reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD=1.26, 95% CI 1.22–1.30), which is a directly interpretable PRS signal, whereas PGS003333 only reports a Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.022 that appears to be a full-model/unspecified metric (no PGS-only R2/AUC) and has covariates listed as Unknown, reducing comparability. Validation sample sizes are similar (39,444 vs 34,703) and do not outweigh the stronger, cleaner PRS-specific effect-size evidence in PGS002759.

For the target trait dementia, PGS000823 has better endpoint fidelity: its phenotyping_reported is "Incident all-cause dementia," directly matching the target, whereas PGS000812 is framed as "Incident dementia" but is reported as an Alzheimer’s disease score and evaluated in an APOE ɛ4-negative context per the publication title, which suggests a more restricted deployment setting. Neither candidate reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so effect-size evidence is the main differentiator: PGS000823 shows a clearer risk gradient (HR 1.36 top vs bottom tertile), while PGS000812 reports only a very small per-unit HR (1.09). Covariates are basic in both (PGS000812 adds PCs; PGS000823 uses age/sex only), with no strong leakage signals. Overall, PGS000823 is more directly aligned to dementia and shows stronger observed stratification despite similar metric limitations.

PGS005170 is the better-supported match to the target trait dementia: it directly targets all-cause dementia with an incident all-cause dementia endpoint and is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR), whereas PGS000812 is primarily an Alzheimer’s disease score (trait_efo Alzheimer disease) with only EUR evaluation. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance must lean on effect sizes and structural/study signals: PGS005170 shows a stronger HR per SD (1.25 vs 1.09) and uses an ensemble/integrative approach with genome-wide coverage (1.32M variants) versus a sparse C+T score with 57 variants for PGS000812. PGS005170’s covariates include APOE ε2/ε4 dosage (a notable packaging/augmentation), but PGS000812 also lacks clean PRS-only metrics and offers weaker effect size and narrower transportability; overall the endpoint alignment plus stronger effect-size/structure evidence favors PGS005170.

PGS005170 is the better-supported match to the target trait dementia because its reported trait and EFO mapping align directly to dementia ("All-cause dementia", trait_efo=dementia) with the same incident all-cause dementia endpoint, whereas PGS000823 is primarily an Alzheimer’s disease score (trait_efo=Alzheimer disease) despite sharing an incident all-cause dementia phenotyping field. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance can’t be compared cleanly; however PGS005170 provides a per-SD HR (1.25) and is a genome-wide, multi-score integrative model (24 component PRSs; 1.32M variants) with multi-ancestry evaluation, while PGS000823 is a sparse 23-variant GWAS-hits score with only a tertile HR contrast and EUR-only evaluation. PGS005170’s covariates include APOE ε2/ε4 dosage (a mild comparability concern), but PGS000823’s lack of PRS-comparable metrics and much sparser construction leaves it less supported overall for general dementia risk.

PGS003576 is the better-supported depressive disorder PRS because it has tighter endpoint specificity (Major Depressive Disorder lifetime; phenotyping_reported: Major depressive disorder) and substantially richer transportability evidence with multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/ASN/EAS/EUR) plus an explicit training cohort (UKB) and training N=67,164. PGS002759 is more weakly supported on visible metadata: it is a generic “Depression” label, has no training sample/cohort information (samples_training N/A; training_development_cohorts empty), and provides only a single European evaluation record with an OR=1.26 (moderate effect) and no PRS-comparable R2/AUC. Although PGS003576 reports only a full-model R² (0.0241) rather than PRS-only metrics, its cleaner covariate set (PCs only) and broader evaluation context outweigh PGS002759’s sparse evidence package.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target EFO (dilated cardiomyopathy), same phenotyping_reported (Dilated cardiomyopathy), same method (PRS-CS), same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, same covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), same training cohort label (HERMES), and same validation sample size (n=347,585). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC/R² are only weak tie-breakers. PGS004862 is preferred because it is the MTAG-enhanced version (trait_reported: "Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)") which domain guidance mildly favors within the same study family, and it also shows slightly stronger reported performance/effect size (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048; OR 1.76 vs 1.56) compared with PGS004861.

PGS002304 is the cleaner endpoint match to the target: both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Follicular lymphoma,” whereas PGS000644 is labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” despite mapping to the follicular lymphoma EFO, creating endpoint-fidelity ambiguity. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so the reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence; still, PGS002304 shows higher AUROC (0.61 vs 0.538). PGS000644 has basic covariates disclosed (age/sex/PCs) and reports additional metrics (pseudo-R², ORs), but its effect sizes are modest and do not outweigh the phenotype mismatch relative to PGS002304’s direct follicular lymphoma endpoint.

Both candidates match the target endpoint well (same trait_efo Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is a direct Dupuytren/contracture diagnosis in both). The key differentiator is PRS-comparable performance evidence: PGS001254 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6646; PGS R² 0.0247, no covariates), whereas PGS001880 provides no PGS-only AUROC/R² and only a partial correlation (partial-r 0.0783), which is harder to compare and less directly interpretable as discrimination. Although PGS001880 has a larger variant set (2443 vs 11) and multi-ancestry evaluation, the absence of standard PRS-only metrics makes its support weaker on the visible fields than PGS001254’s clear PRS-only AUROC/R².

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity to diverticular disease (PGS004614: “Diverticular disease”; PGS004474: ICD10 K57 diverticular disease of intestine) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance is hard to compare. PGS004614’s only discrimination metric is a full-model AUROC=0.76 with explicit covariates including family history (a comparability/leakage concern), making that AUROC less informative for standalone PRS quality. PGS004474 avoids explicit family-history augmentation (covariates unknown) and provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD ≈1.31), giving at least some direct PRS signal evidence; it also has clear UKB development and larger stated training/validation samples. Confidence is low because PGS004474 lacks explicit discrimination metrics and has unknown covariates, while PGS004614 at least reports an AUROC (though covariate-inflated).

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (ICD10 K57 diverticular disease), mapped trait (EFO diverticular disease), ancestry (EUR-only dev/eval), cohorts (UKB), training size (n=174,489), validation size (n=56,192), variant count (1,059,939), and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates—so performance evidence is limited to per-SD OR. PGS004544 has a slightly higher reported OR (1.321) than PGS004474 (1.312), and its method is an aggregated/meta-PRS (“RFDiseasemetaPRS”), which is a mild positive structural signal versus a single-score LDpred2 when other evidence is indistinguishable. The differences are small and metadata are sparse, hence low confidence.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), identical training cohort and size (UKB; n=391,124), identical covariates (basic demographics + PCs), identical ancestry distribution for development/evaluation, and essentially the same reported PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0797 for PGS002092 vs 0.0783 for PGS001880 with overlapping CIs). With performance effectively tied and no PRS-only AUC/R2 available, the structural signals break the tie: PGS002092 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (484,484 vs 2,443), which is generally favored for polygenic disease prediction when other evidence is equal. Therefore PGS002092 is better supported on the visible fields.

PGS000643 is better supported on PRS-relevant evidence: it provides PRS-associated effect sizes (OR per SD 1.133, plus top-1% vs rest OR 2.49) and a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke pseudo-R²=0.00282), with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). In contrast, PGS002304 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.61) with covariates listed as unknown and no PRS-only metrics/effect sizes, making its apparent AUC advantage non-comparable. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both via trait_efo=follicular lymphoma, but PGS002304’s label is exact while PGS000643’s reported/phenotyped label is ‘Nodular lymphoma’; given the stronger PRS-specific reporting and cleaner covariate transparency, PGS000643 wins despite the naming mismatch.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity to diverticular disease (PGS004614: “Diverticular disease”; PGS004544: ICD10 K57 diverticular disease of intestine) and neither reports PRS-only AUROC/R2. PGS004614’s only discrimination metric is a full-model AUROC=0.76, but it is explicitly adjusted for family history (plus age/sex), making that AUROC likely covariate-inflated and non-comparable as PRS evidence. PGS004544, while lacking AUC, provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD ≈1.32), which is at least direct PRS signal, and it has clearly documented training in UKB with a large development sample (n=174,489) and EUR-only dev/eval consistency. Given the covariate-leakage concern in PGS004614 and the presence of a standalone PRS effect size in PGS004544, PGS004544 is better-supported on the visible fields, though confidence is low due to missing PRS-only metrics in both.

Both candidates target primary open-angle glaucoma, but PGS001792 provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209), which is interpretable and below the glaucoma heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0556), whereas PGS004944 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.748) with no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its discrimination evidence largely non-comparable. Endpoint fidelity is slightly cleaner for PGS001792 (phenotyping_reported: POAG) versus PGS004944’s self-reported POAG, and PGS001792 also has explicit multi-cohort development context (BBJ, BioMe, TWB, UCLA). Although PGS004944 has broader listed validation ancestries and a strong OR per SD (1.74), the lack of PRS-only metrics makes it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001792.

Both candidates match the target endpoint well (same EFO; phenotyping_reported is Dupuytren’s disease/contracture). However, PGS001254 comes from a known pan-trait sparse-PRS framework (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely small variant set (11 SNPs), which is a structural warning for generalizability despite having explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² (PGS AUROC 0.6646; PGS R² 0.0247). PGS002092 is a genome-wide LDpred2 score with very large variant coverage (484,484) and is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/EUR/GME/SAS), providing stronger transportability evidence; its reported partial-r (0.0797) is PRS-isolated but not directly comparable to AUROC, so confidence is not high. Overall, the framework+sparsity penalty for PGS001254 and the broader, genome-wide construction plus multi-ancestry evaluation for PGS002092 make PGS002092 better-supported on metadata.

PGS004951 is better supported for dilated cardiomyopathy because it provides PRS-comparable performance evidence (explicit univariate/PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI and delta liability-scale R²=0.101), whereas PGS004861 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.70/0.048) without isolating PRS contribution, which the guidance says is not a valid substitute. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both map to dilated cardiomyopathy; PGS004951’s “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy” is at least as specific, and the “(MTAG)” label is not a negative and is mildly preferred). Covariates are basic in both (no obvious leakage), and while PGS004861 has much larger validation n, validation size is a weak tie-break compared with having clean PRS-only metrics and stronger effect size (OR 1.93 vs 1.56) in PGS004951.

PGS004944 is better supported for the target trait glaucoma because it has higher endpoint fidelity to the clinically dominant subtype (primary open-angle glaucoma) with explicit phenotyping (self-reported POAG) and provides broader transportability evidence: multi-ancestry GWAS input (AFR/EAS/EUR) and evaluation across multiple ancestries with a very large validation sample (n=407,667). Although its only AUROC is a full-model AUROC (0.748) and thus not PRS-comparable, it still reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.74). In contrast, PGS002761 has a more generic glaucoma label but comes from a cross-disease comparison framework context, has only a single EUR-only evaluation record, smaller validation (n=39,444), and provides no AUC/R2 metrics—only a slightly weaker OR (1.68). With both lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, the stronger effect size plus broader multi-ancestry evaluation support favors PGS004944.

Both candidates target the same trait label (Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)), map to the same EFO term, and use the same method (PRS-CS) with EUR-only evaluation. However, PGS004951 provides cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports an explicit univariate (PRS-only) AUC=0.67 (with CI) and PRS delta R² metrics (liability-scale delta R²=0.101), whereas PGS004862 reports only full-model AUROC=0.71 and R²=0.05 without indicating PRS-only contribution (so its AUROC is not comparable as a PRS metric). PGS004951 also shows a stronger effect size (OR 1.93 vs 1.76) and has a larger variant set (1,075,760 vs 709,534) within the same method family. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both; PGS004951’s ‘Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy’ is at least as specific as PGS004862’s generic ‘Dilated cardiomyopathy’. The main drawback for PGS004951 is smaller validation n (7,761 vs 347,585) and slightly different covariates, but validation size is a weak tie-break and the presence of PRS-only metrics outweighs this.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target follicular lymphoma: same trait_efo (follicular lymphoma), same reported/phenotyped label (“Nodular lymphoma”), same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same training cohort (MGI) and training N=3,696, same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and same validation N=3,256. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are weak tie-breakers. On the visible metrics, PGS000644 has slightly higher AUROC (0.538 vs 0.532) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.00349 vs 0.00282) and slightly higher per-SD OR (1.149 vs 1.133), while PGS000643 only clearly leads on the top-1% vs rest OR (2.49 vs 1.48). Given the otherwise identical design and lack of PRS-only metrics, the small but consistent edge across AUROC/R²/per-SD OR favors PGS000644, though the evidence is close.

Both candidates have strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all = gout). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², so full-model metrics are not directly comparable as PRS performance. PGS004160 provides more PRS-relevant evidence via effect sizes (OR per SD ≈2.05 with tight CI; β reported), whereas PGS004768 reports only an incremental R² (0.081) without any AUROC/effect-size context, making the PRS contribution harder to judge. Covariates are cleaner/less confounded for PRS comparability in PGS004160 (covariates=0) than PGS004768 (age/sex/PC1-10), and PGS004160 also shows broader evaluation ancestry (EUR plus SAS) versus EUR-only for PGS004768. Overall, PGS004160 is better supported on visible PRS-relevant fields.

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment to gout (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match). Neither reports PRS-only AUROC/R², so full-model metrics are not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence. PGS004047 provides stronger PRS-relevant support via effect sizes (OR per SD ≈2.0 with CI) alongside AUROC/R² entries (even if full-model), and it is evaluated across two ancestries (EUR and SAS) with a much larger validation sample (n=90,274). In contrast, PGS004768 reports only an incremental R² from a covariate-adjusted full model (age/sex/PCs) with no effect sizes and a smaller validation (n=9,462), making its PRS contribution harder to judge from the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all gout; same publication, same training cohort UKB with n=6,704; same ancestry distribution and validation size n=90,274; covariates=0; no PGS-only AUC/R2 reported so full-model AUROC/R² are only weak differentiators). Given that, PGS004160 has consistently stronger visible performance/effect-size signals than PGS004047 (higher AUROC 0.6936 vs 0.6851, higher R² 0.0893 vs 0.0801, higher OR per SD 2.05 vs 2.00) and also uses an ensemble MultiPRS method (a positive structural signal vs single-score LDpred2). The differences are modest and metrics are full-model, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

PGS001792 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance and study context. It reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209 (and this is below the glaucoma liability h2 ceiling ~0.0556, so it passes the sanity check), whereas PGS002761 provides no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 at all (only an OR=1.68). Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (PGS001792 targets primary open-angle glaucoma; PGS002761 is generic glaucoma), but PGS001792 also shows broader multi-cohort development (BBJ, BioMe, TWB, UCLA) and much larger validation (n=347,396 vs n=39,444). PGS002761’s EUR-only GWAS/EVAL is cleaner ancestry-wise, but the lack of PRS-only metrics makes it less well-supported overall than PGS001792.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target (same trait_efo Hashimoto's thyroiditis, same trait_reported/phenotyping_reported lymphocytic thyroiditis, same method PRSCS, same evaluation ancestry mix and identical validation sample size n=94,651) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With endpoint and design essentially tied, the differentiators are the available effect-size and full-model AUROC signals: PGS005271 shows stronger per-SD discrimination (OR 1.55 vs 1.42; β 0.44 vs 0.35) and a slightly higher reported AUROC (0.630 vs 0.605). Training cohort lists differ slightly, but within the same publication family this is a weak signal. Therefore PGS005271 is better supported on the visible evidence.

PGS001790 is the better-supported choice for the target trait heart failure because it provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.006981), which can be sanity-checked against the trait heritability ceiling and is not substitutable by full-model AUROC. In contrast, PGS005077 reports only a full-model C-index (~0.754) plus an OR=1.452, but no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its discrimination evidence less directly comparable as a standalone PRS. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (heart failure vs congestive heart failure phecode), and covariates are similarly basic; however, PGS001790 also has broader multi-biobank development context and much larger validation (n=358,905 vs n=31,804), which mildly supports robustness when performance evidence is otherwise limited.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_efo=Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=lymphocytic thyroiditis), same publication family, same evaluation ancestry mix (MAE 100%) and same validation sample size (n=94,651), with covariates unknown for both—so phenotype/transportability don’t differentiate. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; the only AUROC shown is full-model and thus not a clean PRS-comparable metric, and the small full-model AUROC edge for PGS005270 (0.639 vs 0.630) is not decisive. The stronger differentiator is PRS signal/structure: PGS005271 uses genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55) than PGS005270’s very sparse P+T score (55 variants; OR≈1.04), which suggests substantially weaker standalone PRS discrimination despite the slightly higher full-model AUROC.

Both candidates have identical endpoint alignment to the target (trait_efo Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported lymphocytic thyroiditis), same publication family, same evaluation ancestry mix (MAE 100%) and same validation sample size (n=94,651), with covariates unknown for both—so phenotype/transportability don’t differentiate. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; the only AUROC shown is full-model and thus not a clean PRS-comparable metric, and the small full-model AUROC advantage of PGS005270 (0.639 vs 0.605) is not decisive. Under the fallback guidance, structural/effect-size evidence matters more: PGS005272 uses genome-wide shrinkage (PRSCS) with far broader variant coverage (1,085,142 vs 55) and shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.42 vs 1.04), indicating materially stronger PRS signal. Therefore PGS005272 is better supported overall despite the slightly lower full-model AUROC.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo = heart failure). However, PGS001790 comes from an explicit portability/framework paper (“Global Biobank analyses…”) which domain guidance penalizes versus a disease-focused heart-failure genetics study; PGS005097 is from a heart-failure–focused Nat Genet study (“genetic architecture of heart failure…”), which is a positive study-archetype signal. On metrics, PGS001790 has a PRS-comparable value (PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.006981, below the heritability ceiling) whereas PGS005097 reports only full-model AUROC (0.72) with no PRS-only R2/AUC, so performance evidence is cleaner for PGS001790. Still, given the strong framework penalty and PGS005097’s broader multi-ancestry GWAS composition plus cross-ancestry method (PRS-CSx) and larger variant count, I select PGS005097, but confidence is low because PGS001790 is the only one with an explicit PRS-comparable R2.

Both candidates map cleanly to hip osteoarthritis via trait_efo and have EUR-only development/evaluation with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so effect-size strength and covariate transparency become key. PGS002763 has a clearer direct endpoint label (Hip osteoarthritis) and reports a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) than PGS004478 (OR≈1.296 with no CI shown), suggesting better standalone PRS signal. PGS002763 also discloses basic, non-leaky covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), whereas PGS004478 lists covariates as Unknown and comes from a ‘risk factor PRS integration’ paper, raising comparability/packaging uncertainty. Although PGS004478 has a larger stated training N and slightly larger variant count, those are weaker differentiators here than endpoint fidelity, effect-size evidence, and covariate clarity.

Both candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity and study context (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = Hodgkin’s disease/Hodgkins lymphoma; same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL; same training cohort MGI with n=736; same covariates age/sex/batch/PCs1-4; same validation n=775) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative. Within this like-for-like setting, PGS000639 shows consistently stronger performance signals than PGS000638: higher AUROC (0.62 vs 0.601), higher pseudo-R² (0.0276 vs 0.0193), higher OR per SD (1.476 vs 1.377), and higher top-1% OR (2.64 vs 1.62), and it also includes slightly more variants (20 vs 16). These aligned advantages make PGS000639 better supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates map cleanly to hip osteoarthritis at the concept level (trait_efo matches), but PGS004478 also uses a direct diagnosis-code endpoint (M16 coxarthrosis) whereas PGS002728 uses the proxy/surgical endpoint “Total hip replacement,” which is more treatment/access/severity-dependent. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS002728’s only visible AUROC=0.66 is a full-model metric with age/sex and is not PRS-comparable, while PGS004478 at least provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD ≈1.30), giving some direct evidence of genetic discrimination. Structurally, PGS004478 is a genome-wide LDpred2 score (~1.06M variants) trained in UKB (n=174,489), which is generally better suited to a polygenic trait than PGS002728’s 44 genome-wide significant variants. Overall, PGS004478 has better endpoint fidelity plus stronger structural/effect-size support, despite unknown covariates and only one performance record.

PGS002763 has better endpoint fidelity to the target trait: its phenotyping_reported is directly “Hip osteoarthritis,” matching trait_reported/trait_efo, whereas PGS002728 uses “Total hip replacement,” a treatment/proxy endpoint that can reflect severity and clinical decision pathways rather than hip OA status. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS002728’s reported AUROC=0.66 is a full-model metric (age, sex) and not comparable as PRS performance; in contrast PGS002763 at least reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.38, moderate signal) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; 1,052,273 variants) versus a sparse 44-variant GWS-hits score in PGS002728, which is structurally less likely to capture polygenic signal for OA. Both are EUR-only, and while PGS002728 is more disease-focused/multi-cohort, the proxy endpoint plus lack of PRS-isolated performance makes it less well-supported overall than the direct hip OA endpoint with reported OR in PGS002763.

Both candidates target the same trait (hypertension) with identical phenotyping_reported (prevalent hypertension), identical covariates (age/sex/PCs plus smoking and BMI), same training n (10,314) and same validation size (39,035), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC ~0.76, which is not PRS-comparable). With endpoint and metric comparability essentially tied, PGS004236 is better supported because it provides stronger PRS-specific evidence via an effect size (OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21) whereas PGS004234 reports no effect sizes, and it also has broader development context (BioMe+MVP+UKB vs BioMe+UKB) and a larger variant set (398,805 vs 234,228), which is a positive structural signal when other fields are near-identical.

PGS005097 is the better-supported match to the target trait (heart failure): its trait_reported/trait_efo are exactly heart failure and phenotyping_reported is a direct HF diagnosis (prevalent heart failure), whereas PGS005077 targets a narrower/administrative phecode endpoint (CHF NOS; trait_efo congestive heart failure). Neither record reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the higher full-model C-index for PGS005077 (0.754 vs 0.72) is not a reliable PRS-comparable differentiator—especially given heavier covariate adjustment in PGS005077 (age, sex, 20 PCs) vs PGS005097 (age, sex, 5 PCs). Study/transportability context favors PGS005097: it is developed across many HF-relevant cohorts/consortia (BBJ, BioMe, CKB, FinnGen, GBMI, HERMES, MVP, etc.) with multi-ancestry GWAS inputs, while PGS005077 is trained only in MVP and comes from a methods-comparison paper. Overall, endpoint fidelity plus stronger disease-focused multi-cohort development outweigh PGS005077’s non-comparable full-model metric.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo are hypertension), but PGS001320 provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.629 and PGS-only R²=0.06493) with basic covariates, enabling a direct assessment of PRS signal and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to thyroid carcinoma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Thyroid cancer”), same publication family, same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL—so phenotype and transportability do not differentiate. Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate Type 2 diabetes) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², so the full-model AUROC values (0.793 for PGS002308 vs 0.825 for PGS000804) are not comparable PRS metrics—especially since PGS000804 uses a more clinically augmented covariate set including BMI.
